walkthroughs.body_html:
World Religions Option — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World Religions Option brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World Religions Option.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Jesus was half God and half human.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Treat others how you would like to be treated.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
